To fit without cutting words or time-stretching, the silent lead-in and the middle of four long pauses between sentences are removed (4.40 s in total). Every removed range is silence (below -34 dBFS).
voiceover.script: What if sending NIM wasn't something that happened after the game, but was actually part of the game itself? That's the idea behind NIM Relay. We turned a real one-NIM transfer into a baton that moves from runner to runner. You receive it, carry it through your relay leg, and pass it forward to another person. Every runner becomes part of the baton's history. Your run is verified by our server, your journey stays attached to the relay, and the next person continues from where you left off. And the world view lets you follow that journey as it grows, instead of treating each game as an isolated run. Here, I'm choosing the baton's next route and its next runner. Then I throw it forward and approve the actual one-NIM transfer inside Nimiq Pay. And this is the part I really wanted the product to make visible. On the left, the sender gets the confirmed handoff. On the right, the next runner receives the baton. There's no fake baton changing hands in our database. A real NIM transfer moves between the two wallets, while NIM Relay records the verified handoff and extends the journey. The new runner can then complete their own leg and send it forward again. Here, that same relay comes back, creating the third verified handoff in the chain. That loop is what everything else in NIM Relay is built around: people, runs, routes, handoffs, and a baton whose story gets longer every time somebody keeps it moving. And every handoff can be checked. These are the actual mainnet transactions behind this relay, with the one-NIM transfers verified onchain. We wanted blockchain to be something you feel through the experience, not something bolted onto it. One NIM. One relay. One journey. How far can we keep it moving?
